summary: The candidate substantively fixes the two reviewed multi-request counterexamples by budgeting the plan path and using request-local K windows with correct global PAGED mapping. It remains a partial fix because a single request-local logits row is forced even when that allocation exceeds the computed budget.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before: 7 failed, 1 passed; budget return, chunk activation, RAGGED allocation bound, and PAGED allocation/mapping regression failed on the prepared base.
Candidate regression: 8 passed on the exact candidate with real GPU FP8/metadata tensors and mocked DeepGEMM/top-k.
4 passed. The independent assertion measured the remaining counterexample: one request-local row allocated 40 bytes despite a 4-byte computed budget; three adjacent existing budget tests also passed.

gpu_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, HIP 7.2.26015. Real device FP8 and metadata tensors were used; DeepGEMM and top-k calls were mocked.
remaining_counterexamples: When one request's group.k_rows * 4 exceeds logits_budget_bytes, max_rows is clamped to 1 and fp8_mqa_logits still allocates one full request-local output row larger than the budget (independently observed as 40 bytes against a 4-byte budget).
remaining_limitations: No GLM-5.3-Flash or RadixArk model weights were available.
The original four-B300 CUDA TP=4/EP=4 serving workload, hierarchical cache, DFLASH traffic, and NVIDIA allocation behavior were not reproduced on the single AMD GPU.
DeepGEMM and fused top-k were mocked, so actual NVIDIA kernels and end-to-end semantic accuracy remain unverified.
No native files changed; native rebuild was not applicable.
